learning: Check s-bend and slalom progress against iteration 6 (0.181 and 0.191). If progress rises above 0.2 with max_error near 0.06 m, mass is a working lever. If oval steering_oscillation exceeds 0.25, the lighter robot is over-responding, so the next step is sensor y 0.03 rather than more kd. If progress does not change, mass is not the limit and the next lever is sensor lead.
notes: Complete robot for the mass test: the Builder's geometry (mass 0.5 kg, otherwise identical to iteration 6) with the iteration 6 controller unchanged. Per-track values are reported for progress, max_error and steering_oscillation, plus the oval finish rate, so the s-bend and slalom can be read separately from the oval.
rationale: Iteration 6 (track 0.10, body 0.10 x 0.12, mass 0.6, sensors x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m, 0.016 m footprint, y 0.05) is the best design so far at 289.8. Its s-bend and slalom progress rose to 0.181 and 0.191, against 0.127 and 0.093 in iteration 4 and 0.132 and 0.091 in iteration 5. Line loss is zero on the s-bend and 0.2 per run on the slalom, and the oval finish rate is 65% with steering_oscillation 0.216. The s-bend and slalom still end off_track at max_error about 0.062 to 0.065, just above the 0.06 m floor. The Builder's geometry changes only the mass, from 0.6 to 0.5 kg, and keeps the rest of iteration 6 fixed, so the race isolates the mass effect. I keep the controller identical to iteration 6 (kp 6, ki 0.05, kd 0.9, base_speed 1.5, weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], last_direction). Lighter mass lowers yaw inertia and raises turn response per unit of turn command, so it should lift s-bend and slalom progress without changing sensing. Oval steering_oscillation is at 0.216, so a rise to above 0.25 is the main risk. kd is held at 0.9 for now because the oval oscillation headroom is limited but not yet breached. Expected result: s-bend and slalom progress above 0.2 with max_error near 0.06 m, and an oval finish rate at or above 55%. This is a prediction, not a measured result.
